headers.//: Everything is revalidated by default. Firebase's own default is max-age=3600 on HTML, and index.html is what names the content-hashed bundle -- so with that default, a visitor who loaded the site in the last hour keeps running the PREVIOUS build and a deploy is invisible to them. The SPA rewrite means route URLs like /results/enrichment-guide carry no extension, so this has to be the catch-all rather than an *.html rule.

Content-hashed build output: the filename changes whenever the bytes do, so these can be cached indefinitely. Listed AFTER the catch-all deliberately -- if Firebase resolves conflicts last-match-wins these get the long cache, and if it resolves first-match-wins they merely fall back to revalidating, which costs a 304 and never serves anything stale.
